searchText: I was listening to an interview with John Adler, and he was saying that the algorithm to find a surround slashing offence is N^2, where I think N is the number of validators (or attestations?). He also claimed N could be several million in the worst case, and it sounded like he was saying it was infeasible to check thoroughly. Is this accurate? Is it possible that validators are doing surround voting and getting away with it because checking is too difficult? https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-surround Hi guys, what top private Ethereum networks are there? Also, do they have scalability benchmarks? *Im basically looking for:* **1.** Top 3 private Ethereum networks **2. **Each one of these Ethereum networks benchmarks in terms of scalability (trhoughput & latency) (graphs & numbers) **3.** Actual benchmark analysis for the public Ethereum networks scalability I'd suggest you start with a literature study on what metrics may or may not make sense for EVM-chains or Ethereum clients. You keep throwing the term "benchmark" around, but that is really rather broad and vague. Same goes for scalability, latency, and throughput. I'd also say that this is not really the server for support questions (like formulating your research question/hypothesis), see the message in <#745072678079168654> . Maybe Ethereum stack exchange or Reddit would be better, but even then I'd still suggest starting with diving into the literature yourself first. Take a look at some Ethereum conference talks/presentations/papers, ethresear.ch, or just browse related/cited papers with scholar.google.com. One general suggestion I'd have is though is to narrow your scope, by _a lot_. interesting, thank you, i will ofcourse read more into it. But when you say `narrow your scope`, can you give me an example? Focusing on a subset of the entire problem, because they each have different bottlenecks. Here's one example of a very influential paper on the topic <@!741734991767142470> https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/broken-metre-attacking-resource-metering-in-evm/ This is a bit more tangential, but covers the interactions of the fee market changes and throughput https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.05574.pdf OMG Tim yes my man This is extremely good, but now im wondering about one thing idk if you specifically know about this but in the first link, i clicked no the video button which took me to their presentation they said they `Replayed transactions and record stats` where/how can i replay and record transactions? There are a lot of ways to do that: either running your own node, using a service like blocknative, or something like hardhat which allows you to shadow fork mainnet. Really depends on what you are trying to do and i can replay transactions from other users? or only my transactions

excerpts.content:

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content:
I'd suggest you start with a literature study on what metrics may or may not make sense for EVM-chains or Ethereum clients. You keep throwing the term "benchmark" around, but that is really rather broad and vague. Same goes for scalability, latency, and throughput. 

I'd also say that this is not really the server for support questions (like formulating your research question/hypothesis), see the message in <#745072678079168654> . Maybe Ethereum stack exchange or Reddit would be better, but even then I'd still suggest starting with diving into the literature yourself first. Take a look at some Ethereum conference talks/presentations/papers, ethresear.ch, or just browse related/cited papers with scholar.google.com. 

One general suggestion I'd have is though is to narrow your scope, by _a lot_.
